_comment: Demo fixture: a short OSCE for an acute chest-pain encounter with three phases. expectedOrder defines the intended workflow.
title: Acute chest pain — OSCE encounter
caseHeader:
A 55-year-old man presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm, beginning 30 minutes ago while at rest. He describes it as a heavy, crushing pressure.

Vitals: BP 145/92 mmHg, HR 102 bpm, RR 20, SpO2 96% on room air, T 37.0°C.

phases.name: History
phases.description: Take a focused history. Select the actions that contribute to your differential.

actions.text: Characterize the pain (site, onset, character, radiation, associated symptoms, timing, exacerbating/relieving factors, severity)
actions.feedback: Correct — full pain characterization narrows the differential between cardiac, pleuritic, and musculoskeletal causes.

actions.text: Ask about cardiac risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, smoking, family history, hyperlipidemia)
actions.feedback: Correct — Framingham risk factors materially shift the pre-test probability of ACS.

actions.text: Ask about associated symptoms (shortness of breath, nausea, diaphoresis, syncope)
actions.feedback: Correct — autonomic features support an ischemic etiology.

actions.text: Ask about recent travel to a tropical island
actions.feedback: Low yield in this presentation — not part of the standard ACS history.

phases.name: Physical exam
phases.description: Examine the patient. Pick the steps that move the workup forward.

actions.text: Reassess vital signs and cardiovascular stability
actions.feedback: Correct — hemodynamic instability changes management urgency.

actions.text: Auscultate heart and lungs (murmurs, S3/S4, rales)
actions.feedback: Correct — new murmur or rales would suggest mechanical complication or heart failure.
